summary: Intermittent pinned-version flip during weighted-slice rollout due to orchestrator snapshot gap
description:
Issue summary:
Customer ByteDock reported intermittent requests being served by the legacy model variant during a weighted-slice rollout that should have preserved per-tenant pinned versions. The symptom is sudden, short-lived 'fallback' occurrences where tenant sessions temporarily receive responses from the older variant (rw-inference-compat-1.2) despite an explicit pin to open-llama-70b-q4.

Impact:
- Affects a subset of tenants on ByteDock's dedicated capacity (prod-us-east).
- Visible as incorrectly routed responses for ~1-3 minute windows, recurring across a 48 minute rollout window.
- Customer reports quality degradation for affected requests; estimated 2-5% of requests for some tenants during windows.

Environment:
- Dedicated fleet: prod-us-east, reserved capacity pool rdw-ded-04
- Control plane: orchestrator v2.18.3; edge-proxy v1.5.9; serving-runtime v3.4.1
- Model variants: rw-inference-compat-1.2 (legacy) and open-llama-70b-q4 (new)

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Start weighted-slice rollout (50% -> 100%) for tenant group A using orchestrator promotion job.
2) Orchestrator writes snapshot to control-plane and pushes route update to edge-proxy.
3) Between snapshot_commit and edge propagation, some requests are observed hitting legacy variant for pinned tenants.

Logs / Evidence snippets:
- Edge routing log (03:12:07 UTC) - tenant t-8892: route_choice=legacy_variant, pin_lookup=explicit(open-llama-70b-q4), snapshot_version=20260310-0311
- Orchestrator commit timeline: commit_start=03:10:52 UTC, snapshot_write=03:11:01 UTC, snapshot_swap=03:11:19 UTC
- Metric: fallback_rate for tenant cohort jumped from baseline 0.3% to 4.8% between 03:11 and 03:14 UTC (dashboards/grafana/dashboard?id=fallback-rate&panel=7)
comments: 2026-03-10 03:30 UTC - Leah Brooks (Support): Customer opened ticket after noticing quality regressions during rollout. Collected request IDs and example transcripts; provided to support. Asked for urgent triage due to production impact.

2026-03-10 04:05 UTC - Marco Chen (SRE): Acknowledged; beginning initial triage. Noted increase in fallback_rate for t-8892. Requested edge logs and orchestrator commit timeline from control plane team.

2026-03-10 04:18 UTC - Ana Ruiz (Customer, ByteDock): Shared request IDs and timestamps. Confirms pins are configured via tenant policy: model_pin=open-llama-70b-q4 and that pins were in place before rollout.

2026-03-10 05:02 UTC - Marco Chen (SRE): Applied temporary edge header enforcement workaround (X-Force-Pin) for affected tenant to prevent routing to legacy variant. Observed immediate suppression of fallback events for that tenant.
2026-03-12 09:10 UTC - Eng (Orchestrator): Deployed staging patch to make snapshot swap atomic; scheduled canary to assess durability. Noted this ticket will be updated after canary results.
2026-03-12 12:00 UTC - Leah Brooks (Support): Informed customer of temporary mitigation and planned code patch rollout; advised on expected timeline and monitoring.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Orchestrator snapshot write completed but edge propagation read an intermediate control-plane state before snapshot swap completed, causing a mismatch between pin map and active route mapping (observed 'slab gap').
Hypothesis 2: Edge-proxy cache TTL on route metadata is shorter than pin-lease acknowledgement window, enabling a brief window where the pin map read returns older cohort assignment.

Evidence: Correlated timestamps show a 18s window between snapshot_write and snapshot_swap. Multiple edge servers reported route metadata with snapshot_version equal to pre-commit value during that window. The fallback spikes align with that window across >3 edge instances.

Testing: Replayed orchestrator snapshot write with debugging instrumentation in staging; reproduced slab gap when snapshot swap used non-atomic replace. Reproduction steps attached in staging runbook (confluence link).
Customer-specific factor: ByteDock's tenant pin TTL had been shortened (custom config) which increased sensitivity to transient snapshot inconsistencies.
resolution: Workaround (applied 2026-03-10 05:02 UTC): Applied X-Force-Pin header at edge for affected tenants to override route selection until control-plane patch applied.
Immediate fix (2026-03-12): Deployed orchestrator change that makes snapshot publication an atomic swap operation, eliminating the observed 18s slab gap during our staging and canary tests.
Edge hardening: Increased route metadata read-retry window and added a short pin-lease grace (300ms) at edge to avoid choosing a legacy variant when snapshot_version is within swap window.

Rollout notes: Patch released to canary pool at 09:00 UTC 2026-03-12, monitored for 2 hours (no recurrence), then promoted to prod pool at 11:20 UTC 2026-03-12. Post-deploy monitoring shows fallback_rate returned to baseline (<0.5%).

Follow-ups: (1) PR #4421 to merge atomic-swap into main and add e2e test covering snapshot atomicity. (2) Add alert to control-plane that triggers when snapshot_swap_latency > 5s. (3) Document tenant pin TTL guidance in runbook and notify dedicated customers about recommended TTLs.
Status: Fix deployed to production; monitoring continuing. Customer ByteDock notified and confirm reduction in incidents. Ticket will be closed after 72h stable observation window.
